messages.author: 7d1ac766483df74a
messages.subject: CFA and invariance of thresholds
parts:
Hello, 
I am trying to assess the measurement invariance using categorical variables for a longitudinal model (different variables for each wave). Is it possible to set equalities of thresholds in Lavaan? If so, is there any example about how to do it?

Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: CFA and invariance of thresholds
parts:
On 04/14/2013 07:15 PM, sebasti...@gmail.com wrote:
> Hello,
> I am trying to assess the measurement invariance using categorical
> variables for a longitudinal model (different variables for each wave).
> Is it possible to set equalities of thresholds in Lavaan?

Just include 'thresholds' in the group.equal argument:

group.equal=c("intercepts","loadings","thresholds")

Hth,

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: CFA and invariance of thresholds
parts:
On 04/15/2013 03:06 PM, sebasti...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thanks. I am using different variables, not groups (e.g., v1_01, v1_02,
> v1_03, v2_01, v2_02, v2_02 ...).

I'm not sure what you need. You wish to constrain the thresholds to be
equal across variables? In that case, you need to label them, and use
the same label for the ones that need to be equal.

Eg (assuming 2 thresholds per variable, ie 3 categories):

v1_01 | a1*t1 + a2*t2
v1_02 | a1*t1 + a2*t2
v2_03 | a1*t1 + a2*t2
...

But perhaps I misunderstood.

Yves.

messages.author: 7d1ac766483df74a
messages.subject: Re: CFA and invariance of thresholds
parts: Thanks. I am just trying to assess different levels of measurement invariance (MI) in a longitudinal CFA. I don't have a grouping variable, I have the same variables measured several times. As far as I know, one way to assess MI is equaling the thresholds of the same variables measured in different times.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: CFA and invariance of thresholds
parts:
On 04/16/2013 04:01 PM, sebasti...@gmail.com wrote:
> Thanks. I am just trying to assess different levels of measurement
> invariance (MI) in a longitudinal CFA. I don't have a grouping variable,
> I have the same variables measured several times.

You could restructure your data so that only have columns for your
measures, and repeated measures are below each other. In addition, there
is a column (say 'time') keeping track of the time points. In other
words, if your data is balanced (same number of repeated measures for
all cases), you can structure your data just like a multiple group
analysis, and use the group.equal= argument. The 'group' argument would
just be your 'time' variable.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: CFA and invariance of thresholds
parts:
On 03/18/2014 08:00 AM, Matthew Browne wrote:
> Hi Yves,
>
> When I try that I get an error:
>
> fit0 <- cfa(model = '
> intensity =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3
> x1 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
> x2 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
> x3 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
> ', data = X)
>
> Error in start[th.idx] <- th.values[match(th.names.lavpartable,
> th.names.sample)] :
> replacement has length zero

Have you declared the x1/x2/x3 variables to be 'ordered' in the
data.frame? If not, you need to say

fit0 <- cfa(model = '
intensity =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3
x1 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
x2 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
x3 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
', data = X, ordered = c("x1","x2","x3"))

Yves.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: CFA and invariance of thresholds
parts:
On 03/18/2014 08:00 AM, Matthew Browne wrote:
> Hi Yves,
>
> When I try that I get an error:
>
> fit0 <- cfa(model = '
> intensity =~ 1*x1 + 1*x2 + 1*x3
> x1 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
> x2 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
> x3 | a1*t1 + a2*t2 + a3*t3
> ', data = X)

In dev 0.5-17, lavaan will automatically assume x1/x2/x3 are 'ordered'
if you specify them as the left hand side of an "|" operator.

Yves.
